{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.45,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R28"],
      "pins": ["R28.1", "R28.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R28 is valued \"24k\" (Resistor_SMD:R_0805). Its own description and LCSC part C2930261 (FOJAN, FRC0805J240TSD) describe a 24Ω ±5% chip resistor, not 24kΩ. The value field and the part metadata disagree by three orders of magnitude.",
      "expected": "A 24Ω resistor between VOUTN and VOUTP, matching the part description and the sourced LCSC part. Alternatively, the part should be re-sourced to a 24kΩ part if 24k is the intended value.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R28\") (value \"24k\") (footprint \"Resistor_SMD:R_0805_2012Metric\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"LCSC\") \"C2930261\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R28 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the BOM follows the sourced part, the value is 1000× lower than the schematic shows. This loads the VOUTN–VOUTP rail heavily. If the schematic is wrong, the sourced part is wrong. Either way the build does not match the intended value.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D21", "D35", "D46"],
      "pins": ["D21.2", "D35.2", "D46.2"],
      "nets": ["NET0153"],
      "observed": "The anodes of three indicator LEDs (D21, D35, D46) sit on NET0153 and on no other node. No supply rail is connected to that net. The cathodes are driven by Ethernet nLED outputs of the CM4 through series resistors.",
      "expected": "Indicator LED anodes should return to the 3.3 V rail (+3V3), as the other indicator LEDs in this design do (for example D1 and D44 use +3V3 on their anodes).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"36\") (name \"/NET0153\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D21\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D35\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D46\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"1\") (name \"+3V3\") (class \"Med Power\") ... (node (ref \"D44\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The Ethernet activity/link LEDs (D21, D35, D46) have no supply path and will never illuminate, so the status indication is lost.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    },
    {
      "category": "other",
      "components": ["Q12", "U42"],
      "pins": ["Q12.2", "Q12.3", "U42.1", "U42.6"],
      "nets": ["+5V", "/5V_FUSED", "NET0102"],
      "observed": "The ideal-diode PMOS Q12 has its source (pin 2) on +5V (also the LTC4412 SENSE node) and its drain (pin 3) on the USB VBUS input net NET0102. The other high-side PMOS switches in the design (Q8, Q13) have their source on +5V and drain on the switched output.",
      "expected": "In an LTC4412 power-path arrangement the PMOS should conduct from the input (VIN/VBUS) to the load. The source should be on the input, with the body diode blocking reverse flow from the load. Here the body diode orientation would pass current from +5V back toward VBUS.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q12\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q12\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "USB input \"OR-ing\"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, U6)"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the source and drain are reversed, the reverse-current protection the USB ideal-diode path is meant to provide may not work, and power could back-feed from the 5 V rail to USB VBUS.",
      "confidence": 0.2
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The clearest deviation is R28, whose value of 24k conflicts with its own 24Ω description and LCSC part. The floating anode net NET0153 (three Ethernet indicator LEDs) and the reversed PMOS orientation of Q12 are lower-confidence concerns."
}

anomalies.observed: R28 is valued "24k" (Resistor_SMD:R_0805). Its own description and LCSC part C2930261 (FOJAN, FRC0805J240TSD) describe a 24Ω ±5% chip resistor, not 24kΩ. The value field and the part metadata disagree by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: A 24Ω resistor between VOUTN and VOUTP, matching the part description and the sourced LCSC part. Alternatively, the part should be re-sourced to a 24kΩ part if 24k is the intended value.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the BOM follows the sourced part, the value is 1000× lower than the schematic shows. This loads the VOUTN–VOUTP rail heavily. If the schematic is wrong, the sourced part is wrong. Either way the build does not match the intended value.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of three indicator LEDs (D21, D35, D46) sit on NET0153 and on no other node. No supply rail is connected to that net. The cathodes are driven by Ethernet nLED outputs of the CM4 through series resistors.
anomalies.expected: Indicator LED anodes should return to the 3.3 V rail (+3V3), as the other indicator LEDs in this design do (for example D1 and D44 use +3V3 on their anodes).
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet activity/link LEDs (D21, D35, D46) have no supply path and will never illuminate, so the status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: The ideal-diode PMOS Q12 has its source (pin 2) on +5V (also the LTC4412 SENSE node) and its drain (pin 3) on the USB VBUS input net NET0102. The other high-side PMOS switches in the design (Q8, Q13) have their source on +5V and drain on the switched output.
anomalies.expected: In an LTC4412 power-path arrangement the PMOS should conduct from the input (VIN/VBUS) to the load. The source should be on the input, with the body diode blocking reverse flow from the load. Here the body diode orientation would pass current from +5V back toward VBUS.

evidence.quote: USB input "OR-ing"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, U6)

anomalies.impact: If the source and drain are reversed, the reverse-current protection the USB ideal-diode path is meant to provide may not work, and power could back-feed from the 5 V rail to USB VBUS.

parsed.summary: The clearest deviation is R28, whose value of 24k conflicts with its own 24Ω description and LCSC part. The floating anode net NET0153 (three Ethernet indicator LEDs) and the reversed PMOS orientation of Q12 are lower-confidence concerns.
